thread:
Sean Gallagher: Kicking off post-incident thread for yesterday’s shadow-runner capacity spike. Goal here: align on root cause + the guardrails we *missed* + owners for follow-ups before we finalize the formal postmortem doc.

Sean Gallagher: Quick recap from SRE POV: GPU util jumped in us-east + eu-west, queue depth went vertical, shadow drops spiked. Primary path stayed mostly ok but we flirted with p99 regressions on a couple clusters. Mitigation was global kill switch + per-route disable.

Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Incident INC-2025-11-shadow-runner-capacity-spike flagged as “Mitigated”. Owner: @Rafael Mendes. Notes: kill switch enabled 16:37 UTC, queue drained by 16:52 UTC.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Timeline from on-call notes:
- 16:05 UTC alerts: shadow_runner.queue_depth + shadow_runner.gpu_util crossing warn
- 16:18 UTC page (queue depth > critical threshold)
- 16:27 UTC we identified a route policy change ~15:55 that increased sampling
- 16:37 UTC global kill switch (shadow_traffic.enabled=false)
- 16:52 UTC queue back to baseline

Rafael Mendes: Primary impact: elevated GPU utilization on shared pools and a few elevated latencies; no user responses changed (shadow isolated) but we ate a bunch of capacity and almost starved the primary runtime.

Cole Summers: Root cause seems to be “sampling misconfiguration” but we should be precise: the policy allowed a per-route `sample_pct` to be set above the tier budget, and we didn’t enforce global caps at evaluation time.

Ethan Park: Yup. We had schema validation (0-100) but no *budget enforcement* by tier/region, and no “safe default” clamping. Policy engine accepted 25% sampling for a high-QPS route.

Benji Okafor: Also: the allowlist was empty in that config. In our docs we said “use allowlist for beta” but it wasn’t enforced. So it applied to all customers on that route.

Jada Williams: The change came from an internal config rollout (intended for 2 accounts). We used the route-level config but forgot the customer allowlist because the UI didn’t surface it + API didn’t require it.

Dylan Brooks: That’s on us on Console/Tooling. The UI makes it too easy to set sample % without forcing you through “scope + budget” gates. We treated allowlist as optional but for beta it should be required (or have a hard warning + blocked in prod).

Keiko Yamamoto: From autoscaling side: the shadow runner pool used the same GPU class as the primary in those regions. When the queue ballooned, it started requesting scale-up, but we hit regional quotas so it just thrashed and increased contention.

Vanessa Ortiz: Fleet side confirms: we were already near the evening peak. Shadow sampling at 25% on that route basically doubled demand for that model family. No headroom, so we spilled into the shared pool and got pressure warnings.

Emily Zhao: Isolation wasn’t violated in code, but operationally we didn’t isolate capacity enough. We said “shadow has strict budgets” but in practice it can still consume shared GPU unless you hard-wall it.

Sean Gallagher: Agree. We should separate:
1) Config correctness (prevent bad policy)
2) Enforcement in runtime (clamp / refuse / shed)
3) Capacity isolation (shadow pool vs shared)
4) Alerting + fast rollback

Logan Wright: Telemetry angle: we lacked an early-warning metric for “effective shadow QPS by route” vs “budgeted shadow QPS”. We saw queue depth, but that’s already late.

Thomas Baird: Also saw cardinality creep during the spike. The misconfig increased volume and we emitted route+model+shadow_target tags at full fidelity. It didn’t take down metrics, but it added load right when we were hot.

Rafael Mendes: On the alerting: queue depth paging worked, but it paged a bit late. We had warn at 5k, critical at 20k. With current throughput, that’s only ~5-7 mins of buffer.

Sean Gallagher: Ok let’s converge on root cause statement draft:
- “A route policy change enabled shadow sampling at 25% for a high-QPS route without customer allowlist and without enforcing per-tier/regional capacity budgets. Shadow runner consumed shared GPU capacity, causing queue depth growth and elevated GPU utilization; primary path latency increased but remained within SLO.”

Ethan Park: Minor edit: “policy engine accepted config; runtime did not clamp; no hard failsafe other than manual kill switch.”

Dylan Brooks: And add contributing factor: “Console did not require allowlist/budget acknowledgement during beta.”

Vanessa Ortiz: Add contributing factor: “insufficient reserved headroom in us-east and eu-west for shadow loads during peak.”

Keiko Yamamoto: Another contributing factor: “autoscaling for shadow worker not bounded by primary capacity signals.” It was scaling based on queue depth only.

Thomas Baird: And “metrics emission not rate-limited per shadow target,” which increased infra pressure (not primary cause but still a gap).

Sean Gallagher: Missing guardrails (list so far):
- Hard cap on sampling by customer tier + route QPS (enforced server-side, not just UI)
- Beta safety: require customer allowlist unless explicitly overridden by admin
- Regional cap + circuit breaker when shared GPU pressure high
- Dedicated shadow capacity pool or strict quota separation from primary
- Early warning: effective shadow QPS vs budget + policy change audit alerts
- Metric/tag allowlists + per-dimension bucketing to avoid cardinality blowups

Cole Summers: For budget enforcement, we should define a single “shadow capacity budget” primitive used by policy engine + runtime. Something like: `max_shadow_rps`, `max_shadow_tokens_per_min`, and `max_concurrent_shadow` at region+cluster.

Jordan Lee: Implementation detail: policy eval currently returns “shadow enabled + sample_pct”. We can extend to return “effective_sample_pct” after clamping against budgets (tier + region). If clamp occurs, emit an audit event.

Logan Wright: +1 audit event. We can pipe it to `shadow_eval.policy_clamp_count` + include fields (route, region, reason=budget|tier_cap|shared_pressure). But we need to be careful with tags.

Thomas Baird: If we do that, please bucket route to `route_group` (or hashed stable ID) and don’t include raw customer_id in metrics. Use logs for full detail behind restricted access.

Rafael Mendes: Action items we need owners for (so I can paste into the doc):
1) Enforce beta allowlist requirement (policy + console)
2) Runtime clamping + shed with clear reasons
3) Separate shadow worker capacity / limit consumption of shared GPU
4) Alerting improvements (effective shadow QPS/budget + faster queue depth paging)
5) Metrics cardinality guardrails
6) Runbook updates + verify kill switch paths

Dylan Brooks: I’ll take (1) Console changes + API validation. Work with @Ethan Park / @Benji Okafor for policy-side requirement. We’ll also add a scary warning modal for sample_pct > 1% even when allowlisted.

Ethan Park: I can own the policy schema + validation changes (2 partially, the clamping logic lives in runtime but policy can clamp too). Benji can help implement + migration.

Benji Okafor: yep I’ll pair. Also propose a “beta mode” flag in policy that enforces allowlist + sample cap globally.

Emily Zhao: I’ll own (2) runtime shed + “never steal from primary” gating. We already have backpressure; we need an explicit shared-pressure signal to drop shadow work earlier.

Vanessa Ortiz: I’ll own (3) with @Keiko Yamamoto. Need to decide if we reserve a small shadow pool per region or enforce via quotas on the shared pool. I’ll post numbers in the capacity channel.

Keiko Yamamoto: Taking (3) autoscaling guardrails. I’ll add an upper bound for shadow workers by region and a rule to stop scaling when primary GPU pressure > threshold.

Logan Wright: I’ll take (4) early-warning metrics + audit event plumbing with @Thomas Baird. We can draft a minimal dashboard panel + alert rule.

Thomas Baird: I’ll take (5) and produce a concrete tag allowlist / bucketing update for shadow_eval metrics, plus a load test gate.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll take (6) runbook update + verify kill switch works without deploy. Also adding a “verification queries” section (queue depth, drop counts, primary p99 spot check).

Sean Gallagher: Great. Please also include in the postmortem “what went well”: kill switch worked, isolation prevented response corruption, we had queue depth alerts (even if late).

Dylan Brooks: Also: we should call out customer comms. Even though no direct outage, enterprise folks will ask “did this affect my latency.” We need a clean statement + pointers to the control plane changes.

Rafael Mendes: +1, I’ll note it and loop in Marissa/Paula separately.

Sean Gallagher: Last thing: can we commit to a concrete prevention milestone? e.g., “budget clamp + allowlist enforcement before re-enabling sampling > 0.5% in any prod region.”

Ethan Park: Works for me. We can set default sample_pct=0, require explicit allowlist, and cap at 0.5% until the runtime clamp lands.

Vanessa Ortiz: Please keep the cap per region flexible; eu-west is tighter. But yes to a conservative global cap in the interim.

Sean Gallagher: Cool. Rafael, once you paste draft into the formal postmortem doc, link it here and we’ll do async edits.

Rafael Mendes: Will do. I’ll open the doc in ~1h and tag owners for their sections.
